response.message: We'll build an Azure reviewer for synthetic PRs: Azure Functions reads only the allowed diff and changed files with a read-only token, Azure OpenAI drafts comments tied to changed lines, and a person reviews them before anything is posted. It never pushes, merges or runs repo code. For the first local test, we run the Functions code with a recorded synthetic diff and a mocked model reply, which only proves the plumbing, line anchoring and refusals. Whether the review is actually good can only be judged later with a real Azure OpenAI deployment that has been approved for your subscription and region, and none of that is verified yet. Should the system post approved drafts back to the PR as comments, or only show them to the reviewer for now?

proposal.title: Azure PR review assistant – first end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: review synthetic pull requests from an existing repository and draft line-linked comments. The flow is PR event → queue → orchestrator fetches the authorised diff and files read-only → screen the content → Azure OpenAI → draft store → human reviewer. Assumptions: the Git host, region, model deployment and access are all unconfirmed. There is no write, merge or code-execution permission. None of these Azure services has native Terraform in this tool yet, so engineering is required. No deployment is implied.

data.label: Existing Git repository
data.description: The existing repository and its synthetic PRs. It stays unchanged. It sends PR events and serves the diff and files to a read-only token scoped to this repository.

data.label: PR event queue
data.description: Holds PR events after webhook validation. Uses a dead-letter queue for failed reviews and deduplicates on PR id plus head commit so the same commit is not reviewed twice.

data.label: Review orchestrator
data.description: Validates the webhook signature, then fetches only the authorised diff and the changed files it needs, within size limits. It builds the prompt, maps findings to changed lines and rejects any comment not anchored to a changed line. It has no write, merge or execution capability, and repository content is treated as untrusted data. It uses a managed identity.

data.label: Secrets
data.description: Stores the read-only repository token and the webhook secret. The orchestrator reads them through its managed identity. No secrets are kept in the diagram.

data.label: Prompt-injection screening
data.description: Screens the diff and file content for injected instructions before it reaches the model. Flagged content is marked and routed to a human.

data.label: Review model
data.description: Analyses the screened diff and returns structured findings (file, line, comment). The model, quota and regional availability are unverified. Local tests use a mocked response.
data.service: Azure OpenAI Service (Azure AI Foundry deployment)

data.label: Draft review comments
data.description: Stores draft comments keyed by PR, commit, file and line, along with their review status and an audit trail. Nothing is posted until a person approves it.

data.label: Human reviewer
data.description: Accepts, edits or discards the draft comments. Posting them back to the PR is an open decision.

data.label: Monitoring
data.description: Tracks traces, failures, token use and dead-letter alerts. Logs metadata only, never repository content.

requirementDrafts.rationale: A token or tool that can write would let a bad prompt or bug change the existing repository.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Retrieve only the authorized diff and relevant files... Never push, merge or execute repository code."
requirementDrafts.statement: The system must only read the authorised PR diff and the changed files it needs. It must never push, merge, change branches or run repository code.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Comments that are not anchored are confusing or wrong. Human approval stops bad AI output from reaching the PR.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "draft review comments linked to changed lines"
requirementDrafts.statement: Every draft comment must point to a changed line in the reviewed commit. Comments that cannot be anchored are rejected, and nothing is posted without human approval.

requirementDrafts.rationale: A mock can show the flow works but says nothing about how good the reviews are.
requirementDrafts.basis: User asked to distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: local tests use mocked model responses to check plumbing only. Review quality must be checked separately against a real, approved Azure OpenAI deployment.

response.message: The emulation found no failing tests, and the design holds together: the read-only boundary, line-anchored drafts and human approval are all intact. It's blocked because none of these Azure components (Service Bus, Functions, Key Vault, Content Safety, Azure OpenAI, Cosmos DB) has a supported code generator yet. The only Azure contract today is private object storage, and squeezing this reviewer into that would drop the scope you asked us to keep. So this isn't something you can fix on the board. It's product engineering work: building native Azure generators for the queue, orchestrator, guard, model and drafts store. This emulation report (revision 2, artifact bcd741b3…) is the test case to reproduce the gaps. While that work happens, let's settle the open decision that shapes the drafts store and the reviewer path: should approved drafts be posted back to the PR as comments, which needs a separate write-capable step after approval, or should they only be shown to the reviewer for now?
